name: Mawkyrwat
description: Headquarters town of South West Khasi Hills district, serving as the administrative and market gateway for the region's offbeat attractions, hot springs, caves, and viewpoints.
facts: HQ of South West Khasi Hills district (formed 2012 from West Khasi Hills)
Located about 78 km from Shillong
Base for visiting Jakrem Hot Spring, Ranikor and local caves
Pincode 793114

name: Jakrem Hot Spring
description: Natural sulphur hot spring at Lawblei (Jakrem) on the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road, popular picnic spot in winter; waters believed to have medicinal properties for bathing.
facts: About 15 km from Mawkyrwat and 60 km from Shillong
Favourite winter picnic and bathing spot
Sulphur water believed to have therapeutic properties
Developed with bathing compartments

name: Symper Rock
description: Unique geological rock formation on the western side of the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road, offering panoramic views of the Mawkyrwat area and surroundings; linked to Khasi folklore with Kyllang Rock.
facts: About 50 km from Shillong on Shillong-Mawkyrwat road
Offers views of Mawkyrwat area
Part of Khasi legend involving battle with Kyllang Rock
Accessible by short trek

name: Umngi River
description: Longest river in Mawkyrwat subdivision, a favourite picnic spot with a small river island used for beach volleyball; source near Sohiong, flows to Umpung lake with scenic rocks.
facts: About 18 km from Mawkyrwat
Longest river in the subdivision
Small island in course popular for volleyball
Stretches to beautiful Umpung lake

name: Phlangja Ud Cave
description: Beautiful cave south of Rangmaw village with stalactites; above it lies grassland offering views of the Bangladesh plains. Approximately 600 meters long.
facts: About 16 km from Mawkyrwat at Phlangja Ud
Stalactites hang from ceiling
Grassland above offers Bangladesh plains view
Cave length about 600 meters

name: Rilang Viewpoint
description: Beautiful valley viewpoint at Mawranglang on the Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road, convenient for picnic and angling along the meandering river.
facts: About 5 km from Mawkyrwat at Mawranglang
On Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road
Scenic valley with river
Popular picnic and angling spot

name: Synrangbah Cave
description: Yawning open cave at Nonglang near Mawkyrwat where the road passes through; provides shelter during rain and is home to bats of various sizes.
facts: At Nonglang, about 3 km from Mawkyrwat
Mawkyrwat-Photjaud road passes through it
Open cave used as shelter in storms
Home to bats of all sizes

name: Dongnob Falls
description: Beautiful waterfall at Photjaud with a cave in the middle that reflects sun rays in winter, creating a splendid natural scene.
facts: About 8 km from Mawkyrwat at Photjaud
Cave in the middle of the falls
Sun rays reflection beautiful in winter
Scenic natural beauty

name: Iawpaw Plateau
description: Beautiful plateau southwest of Nongnah offering bird’s-eye views of surrounding hills, valleys, Bangladesh plains, rivers and Himalayas; legends call it the bed of legendary greens; has one of the longest caves in Khasi Hills.
facts: About 30 km from Mawkyrwat, southwest of Nongnah
Panoramic views including Bangladesh plains and Himalayas
Looks like a bed in legend of legendary greens
Site of long cave in Khasi Hills

name: Ranikor
description: Border town near Bangladesh, former winter resort of the Queen of Maharam; best spot for angling golden mahseer, with Borba Singh Bridge (one of India's longest suspension bridges) and boat rowing; hosts annual tourism festival.
facts: About 45 km from Mawkyrwat, close to Bangladesh border
Former winter resort of Queen Mahadei of Maharam
Borba Singh Bridge second longest suspension in India
Prime golden mahseer angling and boat rowing spot; annual February festival
